newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto Exchange says Bre-X delisted.
newsitem.headline: Toronto Exchange says Bre-X delisted.

text.p: The Toronto Stock Exchange said on Wednesday that shares of Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd had been delisted effective immediately.

"The Toronto Stock Exchange advises that it has completed its review of the listing status of Bre-X...and has concluded that the company no longer meets the required listing standards," the Exchange said in a statement.
"Accordingly, the shares of Bre-X...are delisted by the TSE effective immediately," the statement said.

The Busang discovery -- touted by Calgary, Alberta-based Bre-X as the richest find of the century -- was falsified on a scale "without precedent in the history of mining," according to a report issued late on Sunday by consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd.
Since then Bre-X's stock -- once valued at over C$6 billion -- has collapsed to pennies a share and class action suits loom over the embattled miner.
Bre-X closed up C$0.005 to C$0.09 today on 20 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange, topping actives.
